indication: ** 74-year-old male presenting with abdominal pain and bloating three days status post radical cystectomy. Evaluate for postoperative complications and suspected urinary leak.
technique: ** Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis was performed. Intravenous contrast was administered for vascular opacification. Multiplanar reformats were reviewed.
findings:
**
The liver demonstrates normal size and attenuation without focal mass lesions. The gallbladder is present without wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. The spleen, pancreas, and adrenal glands are unremarkable in appearance.
There is a moderate amount of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity, primarily localized to the paracolic gutters and the pelvis. Within the pelvic cavity, there is a large, complex fluid collection extending superiorly into the lower abdomen, consistent with an extended pelvic urinoma. This collection surrounds the surgical bed and tracks along the pelvic side walls. There is evidence of extravasated contrast material within this collection, confirming an active urinary leak.
The bowel loops are non-dilated and show no signs of mechanical obstruction, although some mild postoperative ileus is noted. The kidneys are normal in position and size; however, there is mild bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, likely secondary to the pelvic fluid collection and recent surgical manipulation.
Regarding incidental findings, there is mild atherosclerotic calcification of the abdominal aorta and common iliac arteries. A small, 4mm non-obstructing renal cyst is noted in the lower pole of the left kidney. There are mild degenerative changes involving the L4-L5 facet joints.
The bladder has been surgically removed. The surgical clips are in expected positions. No free intraperitoneal air is seen to suggest a hollow viscus perforation.
conclusion:
**
Findings are consistent with an extended pelvic urinoma with evidence of an active urinary leak. No associated abscess formation or pneumoperitoneum identified.
